title: रास्वपामा विदेश भ्रमणको मोह बढेको भन्दै पार्टीकै सांसदहरूको खुला असन्तुष्टि

No ads found for this position काठमाडौं । राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी (रास्वपा) का नेता तथा मन्त्रीहरूमा विदेश भ्रमण मोह बढेको भन्दै पार्टीभित्रैबाट प्रश्न उठ्न थालेको छ । पार्टीका सांसदहरूले नै विदेश भ्रमणको औचित्य, खर्चको स्रोत र राजनीतिक नैतिकतामाथि प्रश्न उठाएका हुन् । रास्वपाका सांसद गणेश कार्की, ज्वाला संग्रौला, आशिका तामाङ र राजु पाण्डेले सामाजिक सञ्जाल फेसबुकमार्फत खुल्ला टिप्पणी गरेका छन् । सांसद गणेश कार्कीले संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघीय जलवायु परिवर्तनसम्बन्धी सम्मेलन कोप–३१ मा सहभागी हुन टर्किए पुगेका तथा पुगिरहेका नेपाली प्रतिनिधिमण्डलको खर्चको स्रोत सार्वजनिक गर्न माग गरेका छन् । ‘सधैँ झैँ यसपालि पनि कोपमा जानेहरूको लर्को छ । वातावरणको विद्यार्थी र सांसद पनि भएकाले हो कि धेरै साथीहरू कोपका लागि टर्किए पुगेको, पुग्दै गरेको देख्छु,’ उनले लेखेका छन् । उनले कोपमा सहभागी हुन जानेहरूले आफू सरकारी खर्चमा गएका हुन् कि होइनन् भन्ने सार्वजनिक रूपमा घोषणा गर्नुपर्ने बताएका छन् । ‘जानेहरूले आफू सरकारी खर्चमा गएका हुन् कि होइनन् भन्ने सार्वजनिक रूपमा घोषणा गरून् । गर्नै पर्छ,’ कार्कीले लेखेका छन् । त्यस्तै, सांसद ज्वाला संग्रौलाले सामूहिक रूपमा विदेश भ्रमण गर्नु देश र जनताको हितविपरीत भएको टिप्पणी गरेकी छन् । हिजो अरूले गर्दा गलत मानिएको अभ्यास आज आफ्नै पार्टीका नेताहरूले गर्दा कसरी सही हुन्छ भन्ने उनको प्रश्न छ । ‘हुल बाँधेर विदेश भ्रमण गर्नु देश र जनहितविपरीत छ साथीहरू । हिजो अरूले त्यही गर्दा गलत हुने, आज हामीले गर्दा सही हुने भन्ने कहाँ लेखेको छ ?’ उनले लेखेकी छन् । सम्बन्धित मुलुकले नै खर्च बेहोर्ने गरी विज्ञ तथा सांसदलाई निमन्त्रणा गरेको अवस्थामा भ्रमणलाई अन्यथा मान्न नसकिने उनको भनाइ छ । तर राज्यको ढुकुटी खर्च गरेर विदेश भ्रमण गरिएको हो भने त्यो गलत हुने उनले स्पष्ट पारेकी छन् । ‘सम्बन्धित मुलुकले खर्च बेहोरेर यति सांसद पठाइदिनु, त्यो पनि विज्ञ पठाइदिनु भनेर निमन्त्रणा गरेको हो भने ठीक छ । तर राज्यको धनराशि खर्च गरेर हामी उडेका हौँ भने यो तरिका हिजो पनि बेठीक हो र आज पनि,’ संग्रौलाले लेखेकी छन् । उनले आफू विदेश भ्रमणमा जान नपाएर यस्तो टिप्पणी गरेको नठान्नसमेत आग्रह गरेकी छन् । विदेश भ्रमणभन्दा आफ्नै जनताको आँगनमा पुग्दा बढी जिम्मेवार महसुस हुने उनको भनाइ छ । अर्की चर्चित सांसद आशिका तामाङले पनि राज्यको ढुकुटीबाट सांसदहरूले कति पटक विदेश भ्रमण गर्न पाउने हुन् भन्दै प्रश्न उठाएकी छन् । संसदीय समितिको नाममा हुने विदेश भ्रमणको उद्देश्य र उपलब्धिबारे आफ्नै पार्टीका सांसदहरूलाई समेत जानकारी नहुने गरेको उनको गुनासो छ । राज्यको लाखौँ रुपैयाँ खर्च गरेर गरिने भ्रमणको उपलब्धि के हो भन्ने जनताले जान्न पाउनुपर्नेमा उनले जोड दिएको छन् । भ्रमणको उपलब्धि समुद्री किनारमा फोटो खिच्ने र टिकटक बनाउनेमा मात्रै सीमित भएको हो कि भन्ने आशयसमेत उनले व्यक्त गरेकी छन् । प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाह निकट सांसद राजु पाण्डेले पनि पद र जिम्मेवारीमा पुगेपछि विदेश भ्रमणलाई प्राथमिकता दिने राजनीतिक प्रवृत्तिप्रति व्यंग्य गरेका छन् । ‘जिम्मेवारी/कुर्सीमा पुगेपछि प्राथमिकता त विदेश जाने नै हुँदो रहेछ… अचम्म ! लाज पनि लजायो कि ! कुरीकुरी । जय मातृभूमि नेपाल,’ उनले फेसबुकमा लेखेका छन् । रास्वपाका २० जना नेता तथा सांसदको टोली आज चीन भ्रमणमा जाँदैछ । त्यस्तै, कोप–३१ मा सहभागी हुन नेपालबाट पाँच मन्त्री टर्की पुगेका छन् । भ्रमणको औचित्य र खर्चबारे बहस भइरहेको छ । Kathmandu. Questions have started to arise within the party over the increasing interest in foreign travel among the leaders and ministers of the National Independent Party (NISP). The party's MPs have raised questions about the justification for foreign travel, sources of expenditure, and political ethics. Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) MPs Ganesh Karki, Jwala Sangraula, Ashika Tamang and Raju Pandey have made open comments on social media platform Facebook. MP Ganesh Karki has demanded that the sources of expenses of the Nepali delegation that has arrived and is arriving in Turkey to participate in the UN Climate Change Conference COP-31 be made public. "As always, this year too, there is a rush of people going to the COP. I see that many friends have come to Turkey for the COP, perhaps because they are students of the environment and MPs," he wrote. He said that those who are going to participate in the COPE should publicly declare whether they are going at government expense or not. "Those who go should publicly declare whether they went at government expense or not. It must be done," Karki wrote. Similarly, MP Jwala Sangraula has commented that mass foreign trips are against the interest of the country and the people. She questions how a practice that was considered wrong by others yesterday can be right today by leaders of one's own party. "Traveling abroad while wearing a veil is against the country and public interest, friends. Where is it written that if others did the same thing yesterday, it would be wrong, but if we do it today, it would be right?" she wrote. She said that if the country concerned has invited experts and parliamentarians at its own expense, the visit cannot be considered otherwise. However, she clarified that it would be wrong if the foreign visit was made at the expense of the state treasury. "It is fine if the country concerned has invited us to send so many MPs at their own expense, and that too with experts. But if we have flown away at the expense of the state's funds, this method is wrong both yesterday and today," Sangraula wrote. She also urged people not to think that she made such comments because she was unable to travel abroad. She said that she feels more responsible when she reaches her own people's backyard than when she travels abroad. Another prominent MP, Ashika Tamang, has also raised questions about how often MPs are allowed to travel abroad using state funds. She complains that even MPs from her own party are not informed about the purpose and achievements of foreign trips made in the name of parliamentary committees. She emphasized that the public should know the achievements of the tour, which is being conducted at the expense of millions of rupees by the state. She also expressed her intention to see if the achievements of the tour were limited to taking photos on the beach and making TikToks. Raju Pandey, an MP close to Prime Minister Balendra Shah, has also satirized the political trend of prioritizing foreign travel after attaining positions and responsibilities. "After reaching the position/chair, the priority is to go abroad... Amazing! I'm even ashamed! Kurikuri. Hail, Motherland Nepal," he wrote on Facebook. A team of 20 leaders and MPs of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) is leaving for a visit to China today. Similarly, five ministers from Nepal have arrived in Turkey to participate in COP-31. There is a debate about the justification and cost of the visit.

त्यस्तै, सांसद ज्वाला संग्रौलाले सामूहिक रूपमा विदेश भ्रमण गर्नु देश र जनताको हितविपरीत भएको टिप्पणी गरेकी छन् । हिजो अरूले गर्दा गलत मानिएको अभ्यास आज आफ्नै पार्टीका नेताहरूले गर्दा कसरी सही हुन्छ भन्ने उनको प्रश्न छ ।

‘हुल बाँधेर विदेश भ्रमण गर्नु देश र जनहितविपरीत छ साथीहरू । हिजो अरूले त्यही गर्दा गलत हुने, आज हामीले गर्दा सही हुने भन्ने कहाँ लेखेको छ ?’ उनले लेखेकी छन् ।

सम्बन्धित मुलुकले नै खर्च बेहोर्ने गरी विज्ञ तथा सांसदलाई निमन्त्रणा गरेको अवस्थामा भ्रमणलाई अन्यथा मान्न नसकिने उनको भनाइ छ । तर राज्यको ढुकुटी खर्च गरेर विदेश भ्रमण गरिएको हो भने त्यो गलत हुने उनले स्पष्ट पारेकी छन् ।

‘सम्बन्धित मुलुकले खर्च बेहोरेर यति सांसद पठाइदिनु, त्यो पनि विज्ञ पठाइदिनु भनेर निमन्त्रणा गरेको हो भने ठीक छ । तर राज्यको धनराशि खर्च गरेर हामी उडेका हौँ भने यो तरिका हिजो पनि बेठीक हो र आज पनि,’ संग्रौलाले लेखेकी छन् ।

उनले आफू विदेश भ्रमणमा जान नपाएर यस्तो टिप्पणी गरेको नठान्नसमेत आग्रह गरेकी छन् । विदेश भ्रमणभन्दा आफ्नै जनताको आँगनमा पुग्दा बढी जिम्मेवार महसुस हुने उनको भनाइ छ ।

अर्की चर्चित सांसद आशिका तामाङले पनि राज्यको ढुकुटीबाट सांसदहरूले कति पटक विदेश भ्रमण गर्न पाउने हुन् भन्दै प्रश्न उठाएकी छन् । संसदीय समितिको नाममा हुने विदेश भ्रमणको उद्देश्य र उपलब्धिबारे आफ्नै पार्टीका सांसदहरूलाई समेत जानकारी नहुने गरेको उनको गुनासो छ ।

राज्यको लाखौँ रुपैयाँ खर्च गरेर गरिने भ्रमणको उपलब्धि के हो भन्ने जनताले जान्न पाउनुपर्नेमा उनले जोड दिएको छन् । भ्रमणको उपलब्धि समुद्री किनारमा फोटो खिच्ने र टिकटक बनाउनेमा मात्रै सीमित भएको हो कि भन्ने आशयसमेत उनले व्यक्त गरेकी छन् ।

प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाह निकट सांसद राजु पाण्डेले पनि पद र जिम्मेवारीमा पुगेपछि विदेश भ्रमणलाई प्राथमिकता दिने राजनीतिक प्रवृत्तिप्रति व्यंग्य गरेका छन् ।

‘जिम्मेवारी/कुर्सीमा पुगेपछि प्राथमिकता त विदेश जाने नै हुँदो रहेछ… अचम्म ! लाज पनि लजायो कि ! कुरीकुरी । जय मातृभूमि नेपाल,’ उनले फेसबुकमा लेखेका छन् ।

रास्वपाका २० जना नेता तथा सांसदको टोली आज चीन भ्रमणमा जाँदैछ । त्यस्तै, कोप–३१ मा सहभागी हुन नेपालबाट पाँच मन्त्री टर्की पुगेका छन् । भ्रमणको औचित्य र खर्चबारे बहस भइरहेको छ ।

Kathmandu. Questions have started to arise within the party over the increasing interest in foreign travel among the leaders and ministers of the National Independent Party (NISP). The party's MPs have raised questions about the justification for foreign travel, sources of expenditure, and political ethics. Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) MPs Ganesh Karki, Jwala Sangraula, Ashika Tamang and Raju Pandey have made open comments on social media platform Facebook. MP Ganesh Karki has demanded that the sources of expenses of the Nepali delegation that has arrived and is arriving in Turkey to participate in the UN Climate Change Conference COP-31 be made public. "As always, this year too, there is a rush of people going to the COP. I see that many friends have come to Turkey for the COP, perhaps because they are students of the environment and MPs," he wrote. He said that those who are going to participate in the COPE should publicly declare whether they are going at government expense or not. "Those who go should publicly declare whether they went at government expense or not. It must be done," Karki wrote. Similarly, MP Jwala Sangraula has commented that mass foreign trips are against the interest of the country and the people. She questions how a practice that was considered wrong by others yesterday can be right today by leaders of one's own party. "Traveling abroad while wearing a veil is against the country and public interest, friends. Where is it written that if others did the same thing yesterday, it would be wrong, but if we do it today, it would be right?" she wrote. She said that if the country concerned has invited experts and parliamentarians at its own expense, the visit cannot be considered otherwise. However, she clarified that it would be wrong if the foreign visit was made at the expense of the state treasury. "It is fine if the country concerned has invited us to send so many MPs at their own expense, and that too with experts. But if we have flown away at the expense of the state's funds, this method is wrong both yesterday and today," Sangraula wrote. She also urged people not to think that she made such comments because she was unable to travel abroad. She said that she feels more responsible when she reaches her own people's backyard than when she travels abroad. Another prominent MP, Ashika Tamang, has also raised questions about how often MPs are allowed to travel abroad using state funds. She complains that even MPs from her own party are not informed about the purpose and achievements of foreign trips made in the name of parliamentary committees. She emphasized that the public should know the achievements of the tour, which is being conducted at the expense of millions of rupees by the state. She also expressed her intention to see if the achievements of the tour were limited to taking photos on the beach and making TikToks. Raju Pandey, an MP close to Prime Minister Balendra Shah, has also satirized the political trend of prioritizing foreign travel after attaining positions and responsibilities. "After reaching the position/chair, the priority is to go abroad... Amazing! I'm even ashamed! Kurikuri. Hail, Motherland Nepal," he wrote on Facebook. A team of 20 leaders and MPs of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) is leaving for a visit to China today. Similarly, five ministers from Nepal have arrived in Turkey to participate in COP-31. There is a debate about the justification and cost of the visit.
